title: Integrated network pharmacology and experimental validation to explore the mechanisms underlying naringenin treatment of chronic wounds.
authors: Sun, Rui; Liu, Chunyan; Liu, Jian; Yin, Siyuan; Song, Ru; Ma, Jiaxu; Cao, Guoqi; Lu, Yongpan; Zhang, Guang; Wu, Zhenjie; Chen, Aoyu; Wang, Yibing
one_liner_zh: 该文通过网络药理学和分子对接研究柚皮素治疗慢性伤口机制，虽涉及转录因子RELA和分子对接，但核心是药物-蛋白互作而非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: Naringenin is a citrus flavonoid with various biological functions and a potential therapeutic agent for skin diseases, such as UV radiation and atopic dermatitis. The present study investigates the therapeutic effect and pharmacological mechanism of naringenin on chronic wounds. Using network pharmacology, we identified 163 potential targets and 12 key targets of naringenin. Oxidative stress was confirmed to be the main biological process modulated by naringenin. The transcription factor p65 (RELA), alpha serine/threonine-protein kinase (AKT1), mitogen-activated protein kinase 1 (MAPK1) and mitogen-activated protein kinase 3 (MAPK3) were identified as common targets of multiple pathways involved in treating chronic wounds. Molecular docking verified that these four targets stably bound naringenin. Naringenin promoted wound healing in mice in vivo by inhibiting wound inflammation. Furthermore, in vitro experiments showed that a low naringenin concentration did not significantly affect normal skin cell viability and cell apoptosis; a high naringenin concentration was cytotoxic and reduced cell survival by promoting apoptosis. Meanwhile, comprehensive network pharmacology, molecular docking and in vivo and in vitro experiments revealed that naringenin could treat chronic wounds by alleviating oxidative stress and reducing the inflammatory response. The underlying mechanism of naringenin in chronic wound therapy involved modulating the RELA, AKT1 and MAPK1/3 signalling pathways to inhibit ROS production and inflammatory cytokine expression.
abstract_zh: 柚皮素是一种柑橘类黄酮，具有多种生物学功能，是治疗皮肤病（如紫外线辐射和特应性皮炎）的潜在治疗剂。本研究探讨了柚皮素对慢性伤口的治疗效果及药理机制。通过网络药理学，我们鉴定了柚皮素的163个潜在靶点和12个关键靶点。氧化应激被确认为柚皮素调节的主要生物过程。转录因子p65（RELA）、α丝氨酸/苏氨酸蛋白激酶（AKT1）、丝裂原活化蛋白激酶1（MAPK1）和丝裂原活化蛋白激酶3（MAPK3）被鉴定为参与慢性伤口治疗的多条通路的共同靶点。分子对接验证了这四个靶点与柚皮素稳定结合。柚皮素通过抑制伤口炎症，在体内促进小鼠伤口愈合。此外，体外实验表明，低浓度柚皮素对正常皮肤细胞活力和细胞凋亡无显著影响；高浓度柚皮素具有细胞毒性，通过促进凋亡降低细胞存活率。同时，综合网络药理学、分子对接及体内外实验揭示，柚皮素可通过缓解氧化应激和减少炎症反应来治疗慢性伤口。柚皮素在慢性伤口治疗中的潜在机制涉及调节RELA、AKT1和MAPK1/3信号通路，以抑制ROS产生和炎症细胞因子表达。
